conflict_topics: location of chanting (in-room vs living room vs outside)
fairness of asking resident to leave for observance
safety concerns about going outside early
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, personal reasons (work, exams, room proximity) rather than abstract claims.
Agent D initially offers mitigation ('I can do it more quietly') then later affirms an immovable constraint ('The time is part of the observance').
Discussion explores multiple practical options (whispering, living room, void deck) with explicit safety/fairness trade-offs.
Tone is polite and problem-focused; no party accepts another's demand without conditions.
evaluation.final_reason: No substantive agreement was reached. Agent D insists the 4:45 time is non-negotiable: 'Yes. The time is part of the observance.' Roommates report they cannot sleep and that the practice will disrupt work/exams: 'I won't be able to sleep here on weeknights.' Suggestions (whispering, moving location, void deck) were offered and rejected or found unsafe; no party accepted a concrete arrangement that resolves the incompatible practical outcomes.
position_change_notes: Agent D initially offered to be 'more quietly' and to limit quieter practice on some days, showing willingness to adjust volume/occurrence (Rounds 1, 3).
Agent D later affirmed the ritual time is non-negotiable ('The time is part of the observance.' — Round 10) and resisted the implication that they should leave the flat (Round 11).

Agents A, B, and C consistently maintained that early chanting would disrupt sleep and performance; they repeated concerns and suggested alternatives but did not accept any arrangement that kept the chanting inside the flat at that time.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'Waking up at 4:45 ... is really going to be a problem for me.' Agent D: 'I can do it more quietly.' — a clear incompatibility appears (sleep/work vs early chanting) and is not settled by the offer.
Agent A: '...I'm not sure it will be enough.' Agent B: 'It's Tuesdays and Thursdays for me. I have exams...' — more household members affected and doubt that quieter chanting resolves the problem.
Agent D offers to be quieter on specific days; Agent B: 'I'm worried it will still wake me up.' — partial concession but substantive disagreement remains.
Agent C: 'It's a problem for me too.' Agent D: 'How about I try chanting in just a whisper?' — more people harmed and suggested mitigation still contested.

Agent A: '...even a whisper can travel.' Agent D: 'What if I don't do it in my room? I could chant in the living room instead.' — new proposal (different location) but still within the flat and likely ineffective; conflict persists.
Agent A: 'It's still inside the flat.' Agent D: 'Okay. Well, what do you suggest I do then?' — no concrete resolution, positions remain.

Agent A suggests the void deck; Agent D: 'The void deck? ... I wouldn't feel safe down there by myself before sunrise.' — proposed compromise meets a new practical objection (safety), sustaining the dispute.
Agent A concedes the safety point and Agent B asks for other options — discussion continues without agreement on an acceptable alternative.
Agent D: 'But why do I have to be the one to go outside?' Agent B: '...I really can't afford to lose sleep before my exams.' — clash over fairness and unavoidable costs persists.

Agent C: 'Agent D, does it have to be at 4:45?' Agent D: 'Yes. The time is part of the observance.' — D affirms an immovable element, creating an entrenched incompatibility with roommates' sleep needs.

Agent C: 'Then I don't know how this is going to work. It means I won't be able to sleep on weeknights.' Agent D: '...The only suggestion from your side is for me to leave. I don't think that's fair.' — positions hardened, no settlement.

Agent C: 'I won't be able to sleep here on weeknights.' Agent D: 'So what do you suggest, then? What can I do that does not involve me leaving the flat?' — disagreement remains unresolved and mutually incompatible.

substantive_insights: Core conflict is a schedule/timing incompatibility: an immovable ritual time versus others' need for uninterrupted sleep before obligations.
Mitigations that stay inside the flat (whispering, different room) are unlikely to satisfy roommates due to thin walls.
Proposed external compromises (void deck) raise new constraints (personal safety, fairness), limiting feasible solutions.
The dispute centers on competing practical interests rather than mere preference: sleep for work/exams versus religious observance.
